name: Learning Paths With Teacher Override
title: Learning Paths With Teacher Override
answer: Learning paths with teacher override means adaptive software adjusts what each student works on next based on how they are doing, but the teacher can step in and change that path. This matters because software sees only answers, while the teacher sees the whole student. Teacher judgment should win when the teacher knows better, so a bad day or a skipped important step does not decide a student's course.

sections.body: Adaptive learning paths adjust what each student works on next, based on how they are doing. Programs such as Zearn and Khan Academy do this within a subject. The problem is that software sees only answers, while the teacher sees the whole student. A student might be moved backward because of a bad day, or pushed ahead in a way that skips something important. The teacher override is the fix: when the teacher knows better, the teacher's judgment should win.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, an adaptive path chooses the next activity within a subject from the student's responses. Zearn and Khan Academy are named as programs that do this. For secondary physics, the text reports that personalized learning paths found gains over conventional online learning. The teacher checks the path and overrides it when the teacher knows better. Well designed paths aim to keep students challenged without overwhelming them, and the teacher's job is to check that this is happening for each student.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels the evidence for adaptive systems as showing small positive effects. It says those gains are smaller when compared against other practice software rather than no software, citing Yi et al., 2024, and Letourneau, 2025. A study of personalized learning paths in secondary physics found gains over conventional online learning, citing Ingkavara et al., 2022. In another study, a game that adapted its instructions in real time kept learners working at the right level of difficulty, leading to more learning and less mental strain than fixed instructions, citing Ferguson et al., 2022.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The teacher must be able to override the path. Software sees only answers, while the teacher sees the whole student. A student might be moved backward because of a bad day, or pushed ahead in a way that skips something important. When the teacher knows better, the teacher's judgment should win. The teacher's job is to check that the promise of adaptive learning is being kept for each student.
